data.body:
ROOT CAUSE (established from the six REVIEW_RESULT sidecars on epic 0e68-41eb-5782-4336, before any code change).

Premise correction first — two parts of the hypothesis in the description are FALSE, and saying so matters because they would have pointed the fix at the wrong seam:

1. Scores are NOT carried. The blocking G6 enrichment finding (norm_id n9d22a867f4a4d027) scored validity 0.8 -> 1.0 -> 1.0 -> 0.8889 across the four rounds it appeared in. Pass-2 re-verified and Pass-3 recomputed it every round. The 0.8889 in the final round is 8/9 of the graded set (no_existing_mitigation="no", the rest "yes"); every other finding in that same round also landed on 0.8889, which is what made it LOOK like a carried constant.

2. The review was NOT reading stale material. material_parts["description"] changed on every round (ba10ac32/10135 -> 9aa1e506/7388 -> af4a3972/7927 -> caf24a66/7972 -> caf24a66 -> bb528569/7468), and attest.current_material_fingerprint("0e68-...") today returns 0e6136527d98385c, exactly the final sidecar's material_fingerprint. orchestrator.assemble_context(...).plan_text is 7568 chars and DOES contain the addressing text verbatim ("_build_snapshot (fetcher.py) iterates the configured project set for the base JQL fan-out AND its three enrichment passes -- get_parent_map / get_comment_map / get_issuelinks_map called once per project"). prompts.shared_plan_prefix() puts it in the Pass-2 verifier's context. So the verifier had the refuting provision in front of it and still answered claims_absence="yes" AND absence_confirmed_in_context="yes".

THE ACTUAL MECHANISM — a self-feeding recall ratchet, visible as an empty-evidence signature.

pass1.run_pass1 (src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py, the "Recall" block after the ISF pass) injects each prior concern with a hardcoded `"evidence": []` and `"impact": ""`, keeping only finding/suggested_fix/criteria/location. Tracking norm_id n9d22a867f4a4d027 across the sidecars:

  round 2 (1786610680...): evidence has 3 items  -> FRESH finder output, block
  round 3 (1786611175...): evidence == []        -> recall injection, block
  round 4 (1786612154...): evidence == []        -> recall injection, block
  round 5 (1786612828...): evidence == []        -> recall injection, block
  round 6 (1786613356...): evidence == []        -> recall injection, block

The fresh finder stopped emitting it after round 2 — i.e. the finder DID register that the edited plan addressed it. Every subsequent emission is a verbatim replay. The same signature repeats on nc667728c37b59937 (6 -> 0 -> 0 -> 0), n9f9c21c542f8a621 (5 -> 0 -> 0), ndae84ec4f706d352 (4 -> 0 -> 0): the sidecar accumulates a growing ballast of zero-evidence replays.

Why it never terminates: sidecar.prior_concerns() selects prior findings on `decision in {"block","advisory"}` and `priority >= RECALL_MIN_PRIORITY` only. A recalled finding is re-verified, re-decided as `block`, and re-persisted by build_payload._slim — whose allow-list drops the `_recall` marker — so on the next run it is indistinguishable from a fresh finding and re-qualifies for recall. Recall was designed as a one-shot backstop for a flaky finder ("verdict-flips on IDENTICAL material are a RECALL problem" — sidecar.py:357) and instead became a permanent ratchet. Nothing on the path ever consults material_fingerprint, even though the sidecar records it.

Why Pass-2 does not act as the designed backstop ("A candidate the current plan resolved fails Pass-2 validity and is dropped — recall never blocks on memory alone", pass1.py): the injected candidate is an assertion with NO grounding. review_kernel/verify.finding_listing renders `evidence:` as an empty string, so evidence_entails_finding has nothing to test and the verifier confirms the bare claim. The absence veto in review_kernel/decide.py:660 (claims_absence=yes AND absence_confirmed_in_context=no) is exactly the right lever and never fires, because the verifier answers absence_confirmed_in_context="yes" on an evidence-less restatement rather than searching the plan for the refuting provision. v2 sidecars DO persist evidence losslessly (story 4e19) — prior_concerns simply never reads it.

FIX SHAPE (all three confined to the recall path; fresh-finding verification untouched):
(a) prior_concerns carries the persisted `evidence` (and `impact`) into the concern, and run_pass1 injects them, so Pass-2 re-grounds the claim's original quotes against the CURRENT plan instead of rubber-stamping a bare assertion;
(b) a prior finding with NO persisted grounding evidence is INELIGIBLE for recall — there is nothing to re-ground it with, and that set is exactly the previous recall injections, which breaks the ratchet (and works on the already-written sidecars, no migration);
(c) recall is suppressed wholesale when the prior sidecar's material_fingerprint differs from attest.current_material_fingerprint() — on CHANGED material the fresh finder's silence is evidence the edit resolved the finding, not a miss, which is recall's own stated contract.
Plus: persist `recalled` in build_payload._slim so the ratchet is visible offline, and record the suppression reason in coverage.

Related prior work checked, none touched: 1656 (completion_tool_policy per-kind claim) and 1700 (completion verifier store pinning) are on the completion-verifier path; the sidecar margin work is in decision_margin/_slim's scoring fields, not the eligibility filter.
